entries.name: Big Banana

facts.claim: Big Banana Fun Park is at 351 Pacific Hwy, Coffs Harbour; the park, gift shop and Going Bananas Cafe are open every day except Christmas Day, opening at 9 am, with each ride on its own session times.
The Big Banana photo is free all year, spectators enter free and the cafe needs no ticket; rides are paid (Go Bananas Fun Pass from A$53.50, Ultimate Pass day ticket).
The Big Banana opened on 22 December 1964 and is described as Australia's original 'Big Thing'.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Page title: 'The Big Banana Fun Park | Coffs Harbour Attractions & Activities'. Loaded OK.
unverified: Closing time (5 PM) is Wikivoyage's, not the operator's; the operator gives 'opens 9 am' and per-attraction session times on its Fun Park Info page (URL not found by guessing).
Cost recorded as free because the Banana photo, cafe and gift shop need no ticket; rides are extra (pass from A$53.50 on the operator's home page).

entries.name: Muttonbird Island

facts.claim: NPWS: Muttonbird Island (Giidany Miirlarl) Nature Reserve is always open but may close at times for poor weather or fire danger; one of few easily accessible places in NSW where wedge-tailed shearwaters nest.
Wikivoyage: the walk over the island is 10-20 minutes, steep with no shade; eastern side has sea views and whales can be seen at some times of year; shearwaters nest from about November.
NPWS offers a guided 'Muttonbirds by Moonlight' evening tour and a free self-guided audio tour in the NPWS app.

unverified: No entry fee is listed on the NPWS page (treated as free); the moonlight tour price was not checked.
Walk 'starts at the breakwall ~-30.3038,153.1445' per placement; pin kept on the island itself (OSM place=islet / nature_reserve, HIGH).

entries.name: Park Beach

facts.claim: Park Beach is the main beach in Coffs, just north of the mouth of Coffs Creek; a surf beach where swimming can be rough.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Public beach, no single steward.
entries.coordinates_source: Tool says LOW only because the Wikipedia point (-30.2897,153.1189) is ~2 km inland and wrong; the OSM natural=beach feature is the same as the placement point.
unverified: Patrol times not checked.

entries.name: Bongil Bongil National Park

facts.claim: NPWS: near Coffs Harbour on the NSW north coast, good for fishing and barbecues, and home to one of NSW's largest koala populations (important koala habitat).
NPWS: the park is always open but may close at times for poor weather or fire danger; activities include walking, paddling, cycling, fishing and picnics.

entries.coordinates_source: Placement point is OSM Bongil Beach Trail (visitor access); tool returned only the park-area centroid (-30.4126,153.0655, LOW), 1.2 km away, so the visitor-access point is kept. Not a HIGH/MEDIUM tool result: owner to confirm.
unverified: No park entry fee shown on the NPWS page (Hat Head's page shows one, this one does not); treated as free.
Visit duration is the proposer's estimate.

entries.name: Woolgoolga

facts.claim: Woolgoolga ('Woopi') is a relaxed coastal town known for long sandy beaches and strong Sikh heritage, a stop on the Pacific Highway and a gateway to quieter coast.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Town, no single steward.
entries.coordinates_source: Town point (OSM place=locality, matches placement).

entries.name: Guru Nanak Sikh Temple

facts.claim: One of the largest Sikh temples in regional Australia; visitors are welcome outside prayer times, dress modestly; 1-13 River St, Woolgoolga.
Woolgoolga Heritage Walk lists the temple open to visitors 9 am to 6 pm, seven days a week, phone (02) 6654 0099; shoes off and head covered inside (cloths provided).

entries.ticketUrl_note: No official temple website found; heritage-walk and Wikivoyage pages are not the steward.
entries.coordinates_source: Tool found no OSM feature (LOW). Point kept = the Wikivoyage listing's own geotag (-30.11715,153.19285), 40 m from the placement point (OSM place_of_worship by proposer). Two sources agree.
unverified: Hours come from a community heritage-walk site, not the temple; one older guide says weekends only. Phone to confirm.
Admission assumed free (place of worship); no price source.

entries.name: Woolgoolga Beach

facts.claim: A wide, clean stretch of sand ideal for swimming, surfing and long walks; the headland gives views up and down the coast, especially at sunrise.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Public beach.
entries.coordinates_source: OSM natural=beach point (placement); Wikivoyage listing point (-30.0986,153.2011) is 700 m north along the same long beach. Beach is long; kept OSM point.

entries.name: Arrawarra Beach

facts.claim: Arrawarra is a quiet coastal locality just north of Woolgoolga, known for uncrowded beaches and consistent surf.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Public beach.
entries.coordinates_source: OSM natural=beach (placement); tool LOW because Commons median is 309 m away.
unverified: Only a single counted source (Wikivoyage Woolgoolga); marginal.

entries.name: Coffs Coast Wildlife Sanctuary

facts.claim: Operator: 65 Orlando Street, Coffs Harbour NSW; open daily 9 am to 3 pm; cafe open until 2 pm; day ticket adults $52, family $152.50.
Operator: a not-for-profit rescue, rehabilitation and release sanctuary where visitors can see dolphins, penguins, sea lions and turtles.
Wikivoyage's 'Dolphin Marine Magic' listing is on Orlando Street near the jetty end of Coffs Harbour (same site).

entries.ticketUrl_note: Page title: 'Coffs Harbour Day Out | Coffs Coast Wildlife Sanctuary'. Loaded OK (redirect from .com.au domain to .org.au).
entries.coordinates_source: resolve-pin.py gave only LOW (photon landuse=retail -30.298763,153.136392; Commons median -30.298055,153.135559 from 43 files, ~110 m apart). Used the Wikivoyage listing geotag for the same Orlando St site (-30.29831,153.136689): within ~60-130 m of both. Operator page gives the address only, no map point. Owner to check on a map.
entries.bio_suggestion: A not-for-profit rescue sanctuary on the former Dolphin Marine Magic site, with dolphins, penguins, sea lions and turtles.
unverified: Standalone id 'coffs-coast-wildlife-sanctuary' is a suggestion (placement had no declined-proposal id).
Visit duration (2-3 h) is the proposer's estimate.

Sanctuary is the former Dolphin Marine Magic: the renaming is shown by the operator-site title and the skeptic note; the operator page does not itself say 'formerly'. Wikivoyage still lists Dolphin Marine Magic (adults $27, 9-4), which is out of date.

entries.name: Port Macquarie Koala Hospital

facts.claim: Koala Conservation Australia: the Lord Street site (154 Lord Street, Port Macquarie) reopens Monday 7 September 2026 after redevelopment, open daily 8:30 am to 4 pm except Christmas Day.
Visitors can see resident koalas, exhibits and the koala clinic; the hospital was temporarily based at the Wild Koala Breeding Visitor Centre, Guulabaa, during the works.
An entry fee was introduced from 16 September 2024 (amount not stated on the page found).
VisitNSW: the Lord Street Koala Hospital has reopened after a $10.7 million redevelopment.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Page title: 'Visit the world-famous Port Macquarie Koala Hospital! - Koala Conservation Australia'. Loaded OK. Ticket shop deep links 404, so the hospital page is linked.
entries.coordinates_source: OSM amenity=animal_shelter 'Koala Hospital' (placement point), next to Roto House (-31.4426,152.9194); tool LOW because Commons median is 1.3 km off (town photos). Address 154 Lord St matches.
entries.bio_suggestion: A working koala hospital on Lord Street, reopened in 2026, where visitors see resident koalas and the clinic.
unverified: Adult price A$12.50 is from visitor reviews (search snippets), not the operator: confirm. Operator pages show 'Buy Tickets' with no amount.
Bio should drop 'daily public viewing of patients' wording: viewing areas and clinic, entry fee applies.
Closed Christmas Day (operator).

entries.name: Sea Acres National Park

facts.claim: NPWS: Sea Acres Rainforest Centre open 9 am to 4:30 pm daily, closed Christmas Day; the park is always open but may close for weather or fire.
NPWS: the Sea Acres Rainforest boardwalk is a 1.3 km loop, 27 min to 1 h 15 suggested, adult $9, child $5, family $20, pension/seniors $7.
NPWS also runs a ranger-guided Aboriginal culture tour along the boardwalk.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Page title: 'Sea Acres National Park | NSW National Parks'. Loaded OK.
entries.coordinates_source: Pin is the Sea Acres Rainforest Centre visitor entrance (Wikivoyage listing -31.4617,152.9301; placement -31.46158,152.93; Wikipedia -31.4639,152.9314). Tool LOW only because OSM park centroid (-31.4662) is a bureaucratic centroid.
unverified: NPWS shows a 'Closed areas' alert on the boardwalk page; check before visiting.
Visit 1.25 h max from NPWS 'suggested' time; tours take longer.

entries.name: Tacking Point Lighthouse

facts.claim: Council: Tacking Point Lighthouse, built 1879 and restored, stands in a reserve with 180-degree ocean and coast views, an accessible walkway and whale-watching lookouts.
Lighthouses of Australia: the reserve is open all year but the tower itself is closed to the public.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Council page titled 'Tacking Point Lighthouse Reserve'. Loaded OK. Council is the steward.
unverified: 'Open 24 hours' is inferred from an open public reserve; no stated hours found.
Tower is closed to the public: bio should say views from the reserve, not the lighthouse interior.

entries.name: Port Macquarie Coastal Walk

facts.claim: NPWS: 9 km one way, Grade 4, 3-4 hours suggested; sections Westport to Town Beach 2 km, Town Beach to Flynns Beach 2.2 km, Flynns Beach to Shelly Beach 2.2 km, Shelly Beach to Tacking Point 2.7 km.
Whale migration May to November can be seen from the walk.

entries.ticketUrl_note: NPWS walking-track page, title 'Port Macquarie coastal walk | NSW National Parks'. Loaded OK.
entries.coordinates_source: Midpoint of OSM route relation 14223022 computed by the proposer (-31.45519,152.93213), near Shelly Beach, consistent with the 4.5 km half-way of a 9 km walk (Flynns to Shelly sections). resolve-pin returned LOW (only the 'Coastal Walk' steps); route-relation midpoint kept. Owner to spot-check.
entries.bio_suggestion: A 9 km coastal walk from Westport Park past beaches and headlands to Tacking Point Lighthouse, split into four sections.
unverified: NPWS shows Safety and Closed-areas alerts on the page; the Sea Acres section can be closed.
Sea Acres section is closed to dogs.

entries.name: Shelly Beach

facts.claim: Shelly Beach lies next to Sea Acres, with good waves at the northern end and a semi-protected rock pool for snorkelling and children at the south; barbecue areas, no food stores; parking is hard.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Public beach.
entries.coordinates_source: OSM natural=beach (placement); Wikivoyage geotag is -31.4583,152.9329 (~370 m north-east, same beach).

entries.name: Flynns Beach

facts.claim: Flynns Beach is in the resort precinct, a tourist beach with good surf, patrolled areas all summer, shade under Norfolk pines and a cafe; parking is hard in summer.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Public beach.
entries.coordinates_source: OSM natural=beach (placement).

entries.name: Town Beach

facts.claim: Town Beach is Port Macquarie's most central beach; the south end is patrolled and family-friendly with a beachfront cafe, the north end has currents and submerged rocks.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Public beach.
entries.coordinates_source: OSM natural=beach (placement); Wikivoyage geotag -31.4302,152.9197 is within 250 m.

entries.name: Roto House

facts.claim: NPWS: late-Victorian 11-room red-mahogany house built in 1891 by surveyor John Flynn, occupied by the family until 1979, maintained by NPWS; 2 Roto Place, Port Macquarie; picnic lawns and an onsite cafe.
Wikivoyage: open daily 10 am to 4:30 pm, closed Christmas Day, Easter Sunday and Anzac Day morning.
Koala Conservation Australia: the Roto cafe is open 7 days, 8 am to 4:30 pm Dec-Feb and 8:30 am to 3 pm Mar-Nov.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Page title: 'Roto House | NSW National Parks'. Loaded OK.
entries.bio_suggestion: An 1891 red-mahogany heritage house in Macquarie Nature Reserve, with lawns, a cafe and the koala hospital next door.
unverified: Hours are Wikivoyage's: the NPWS page gives no house hours (only a contact line). 'Free guided tours' in the proposer's bio is NOT supported by any source found; drop it.
No admission price found on NPWS (treated as free).

entries.name: Billabong Zoo

facts.claim: Open every day 9 am to 5 pm except Christmas Day; over 80 species and 200 animals on a 10-acre koala and wildlife park; free zoo talks through the day.
Ticket prices: adult $49, child 3-14 $32, pensioners $45, family (2 adults, 2 children) $149.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Page title: 'Billabong Zoo | Port Macquarie Koala and Wildlife Park'. Loaded OK.
entries.coordinates_source: OSM tourism=zoo, Wikipedia point 129 m away (effectively MEDIUM-HIGH).
unverified: Visit duration is the proposer's estimate.

entries.name: Skywalk

facts.claim: NPWS: Skywalk lookout offers views over Dorrigo National Park and the Bellinger Valley to the coast; open during the day, closing between 10 pm and 5 am.
NPWS visitor centre hours: 9 am to 4:30 pm September-May, 9 am to 3:30 pm June-August, closed Christmas Day.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Page title: 'Skywalk lookout | NSW National Parks'. Loaded OK.
entries.coordinates_source: OSM tourism=viewpoint, matches Wikivoyage geotag (-30.36366,152.7299): HIGH.
unverified: No fee on the NPWS page; Wikivoyage (2021) mentions a $2 donation at the rainforest centre, unconfirmed.
Visit duration is the proposer's estimate.

entries.name: Wonga Walk

facts.claim: NPWS: Wonga walk is a 5.8 km loop, Grade 3 (hard), 2-3 hours suggested, through subtropical rainforest past Tristania and Crystal Shower falls; collect a map at the Dorrigo Rainforest Centre.

NPWS shows no closure on the walk page (one 'Other planned events' alert); a 2025 construction closure of the Tristania Falls sections has been reported as ended and the walk reopened after access upgrades.
Dorrigo Rainforest Centre hours 9 am to 4:30 pm Sep-May, 9 am to 3:30 pm Jun-Aug; closed Christmas Day.

entries.hours: Daylight; visitor centre 9 AM – 4:30 PM (to 3:30 PM Jun–Aug)
entries.ticketUrl_note: Page title: 'Wonga walk | NSW National Parks'. Loaded OK.
entries.coordinates_source: Midpoint of OSM hiking route relation 6265960 (proposer's computation), lying between the Skywalk and Crystal Shower Falls, consistent. resolve-pin timed out on this one.
entries.bio_suggestion: A 5.8 km rainforest loop past Crystal Shower and Tristania falls in Dorrigo National Park, allow two to three hours.
unverified: Reopening after 2025 works is from a secondary report plus the absence of a closure on the NPWS page; read the NPWS alert before going.
The walk is 5.8 km on NPWS but ~6 km on OSM; bio's 'two-hour' should read 2-3 hours.

entries.name: Dangar Falls

facts.claim: Dangar Falls is a 30 m cascade across the Bielsdown River, about 1.2 km north of Dorrigo; small, picturesque and a popular photography spot.
Wikipedia notes the waterhole has been the scene of fatal accidents and that council signs warn against jumping.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Public lookout on council land, no single steward.
entries.coordinates_source: OSM waterway=waterfall matches Wikipedia within 20 m: HIGH.
unverified: Viewing platform and 24-hour access assumed; no steward page found.

entries.name: Crystal Shower Falls

facts.claim: NPWS: Crystal Shower Falls walk is 3.2 km return, Grade 3, 1 h to 1 h 30; a suspension bridge crosses in front of the falls and a short side track leads behind the waterfall into a rocky cavern.
It starts from The Glade picnic area and is part of the Wonga walk circuit; no wheelchair access.
Wikivoyage (2021) says you can no longer go behind the falls: conflicts with the current NPWS page.

entries.hours: Daylight; visitor centre 9 AM – 4:30 PM (to 3:30 PM Jun–Aug)
entries.ticketUrl_note: Page title: 'Crystal Shower Falls | NSW National Parks'. Loaded OK.
entries.coordinates_source: HIGH: the placement's Wikivoyage point is confirmed by OSM waterway=waterfall (-30.380691,152.729527) and Commons median 23 m away; pin moved 14 m to the OSM node.
entries.bio_suggestion: A 3.2 km return rainforest walk in Dorrigo National Park to a waterfall you cross by suspension bridge and can walk behind.
unverified: Whether the track behind the falls is open today: NPWS page says yes, Wikivoyage 2021 says no. NPWS alert on the page was 'Other planned events'.
Bio: it is a 3.2 km return walk (Grade 3) to the falls, not just 'a large waterfall'; suggest including the walk.

entries.name: Dorrigo

facts.claim: Dorrigo is a small plateau town on Waterfall Way (B78), 30 min from Bellingen, 1 h from Coffs Harbour, known as the town of waterfalls.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Town, no single steward.
entries.coordinates_source: OSM place=locality (HIGH with Commons median).
unverified: Marginal as a spot: a gateway town with Dangar Falls and the national park as the real draws.

entries.name: Bellingen

facts.claim: Bellingen is a pretty town of about 13,000 in a green valley, slightly alternative, with arts, crafts and markets; the Waterfall Way Visitor Centre is at 29-31 Hyde St.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Town, no single steward.
entries.coordinates_source: OSM place=locality, same as placement; tool LOW only because no second source for a town.
unverified: Markets run only on set days (not a spot).

entries.name: Glenifer Road Swimming Hole

facts.claim: Wikivoyage: take the first left after Glenifer hall, park at the first bridge, walk about 300 m upstream along the river to a deep swimming hole.

Guide sites place the swimming spots on the Never Never River, about 12 km north-west of Bellingen, via a 500 m return walk with a rope swing; one local reports some online directions lead onto private land.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Informal swimming hole, no steward.
unverified: PIN UNRESOLVED: the placement point (-30.4425,152.8930) is a point on Gleniffer Road about 3 km from Gleniffer Hall (-30.3883,152.8842); the real hole is by the first bridge after the turn past the hall. No OSM feature, Wikipedia or Commons point for it; resolve-pin found nothing.
Access may cross private land and the river has had fatalities; low confidence this is a stable, public place. Recommend HOLD for owner review rather than add.
Single counted source (Wikivoyage Bellingen); name spelling 'Glenifer' vs locality 'Gleniffer'.

entries.name: Trial Bay Gaol

facts.claim: NPWS: open 9 am to 4:30 pm daily, closed Christmas Day; self-guided entry adult $11, concession $8, family $30; allow about 1 hour.
The gaol opened in 1886 after 13 years of construction to house labourers building a breakwater; today a picturesque ruin with a museum and memorial inside Arakoon National Park.
Wikipedia: heritage-listed former public works prison and internment camp at Arakoon, Kempsey Shire.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Page title: 'Trial Bay Gaol | NSW National Parks'. Loaded OK.
entries.coordinates_source: HIGH (OSM tourism=historic + Wikipedia 40 m).
unverified: Arakoon NP page lists no separate vehicle fee.

entries.name: Smoky Cape Lighthouse

facts.claim: NPWS: lighthouse at 446 Lighthouse Road, Arakoon, in Hat Head National Park; a short but steep climb; NPWS ranger-led lighthouse tours; park entry fee $8 per vehicle per day; park always open.
Wikipedia: built 1891, 111 m above the sea, the highest lighthouse light in NSW; first NPWS lighthouse opened for tours (1998).

entries.ticketUrl_note: Page title: 'Smoky Cape lighthouse | NSW National Parks'. Loaded OK.
entries.coordinates_source: HIGH (OSM man_made=lighthouse + Wikipedia 13 m).
unverified: $8 is per vehicle per day (Hat Head park entry), not per adult; NPWS shows a 'Closed areas' alert.
Tour prices/times not fetched; 'Open 24 hours' refers to the park; whether the lighthouse grounds are open round the clock was not stated.

entries.name: Arakoon National Park

facts.claim: NPWS: beachside camping, rocky foreshores with fishing, and sheltered beaches for swimming, snorkelling and whale watching (July-August); home to Trial Bay Gaol; park always open.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Page title: 'Arakoon National Park | NSW National Parks'. Loaded OK.
entries.coordinates_source: Placement point is the OSM nature_reserve point beside Trial Bay (LOW from tool: area centroid, 0 m from hint); the visitor area (Front Beach / Trial Bay campground) is within ~500 m. Accepted as the park's visitor point; owner to confirm.
unverified: No park entry fee shown on the NPWS page; Trial Bay Gaol charges separately ($11).
Overlaps Trial Bay Gaol (a near-duplicate risk, 500 m apart): consider folding the gaol and park.
